complexity.notes: Correct but does one full pass per height value (~10001 passes under the stated cap), which is why it hits the size ladder's time cap near n = 2**13. A true O(n) single pass exists using ||a monotonic increasing stack of indices, where each pop computes that bar's maximal rectangle width directly||. Style: using one variable (`largest`) for both the initial max height and the running best area is confusing; a separate name would read better, and the duplicated area-update after the inner loop could be folded in by iterating runs more carefully.
complexity.summary: Brute-force sweep: for every height level i from 0 to max(heights), it makes a full pass finding the widest run of consecutive bars at least i tall and tracks the best area i * width. Reusing `largest` first as the sweep bound and then as the best area works only because range() is evaluated once up front.
